properties.natural_language: All incoming P2P block data requests (GetBlockBodies, GetReceipts) MUST be validated to confirm the requested block number is >= 15,537,393 (Paris upgrade boundary) before processing.
The eth/70 protocol message handler MUST validate the message format conforms to the eth/70 protocol specification before interpreting block number fields.

GetBlockBodies (0x05) and GetReceipts (0x0f) message handlers MUST reject requests targeting blocks below the Paris upgrade boundary (block 15,537,393) and MUST apply rate limiting on request volume to prevent resource exhaustion.
The rejection mechanism for pre-PoS data requests MUST be defined: either silent drop (no response) or explicit error. The implementation MUST be consistent across all message types.
When pre-PoS data is unavailable via eth/70, an alternative fallback mechanism (archive nodes or Era files) MUST be available and documented for clients requiring historical data.
In a mixed eth/69 and eth/70 network, protocol interactions MUST NOT introduce DoS vectors. Peers on different protocol versions MUST handle version mismatches gracefully.
Block 15,537,393 MUST be used as the exact Paris upgrade boundary for all block number range checks. This value MUST NOT be configurable or overridable.
The client MUST be able to reliably distinguish PoS from pre-PoS block numbers using the fixed Paris boundary, without relying on external oracle data.
Light clients operating on post-PoS data MUST NOT require pre-PoS historical data for verification of current state.
After a protocol upgrade from eth/69 to eth/70 completes, the client MUST refuse to serve any block bodies or receipts for blocks before 15,537,393.
After ACTION-CHECK-BLOCK-NUMBER determines a request targets post-PoS data (block >= 15,537,393), the system MUST transition to STATE-REQUEST-POST-POS and the data MUST be served if available.
After ACTION-CHECK-BLOCK-NUMBER determines a request targets pre-PoS data (block < 15,537,393), the system MUST transition to STATE-REQUEST-PRE-POS and the request MUST be rejected.
After message scope validation, messages targeting blocks >= 15,537,393 MUST be marked as MSG-VALID; messages targeting blocks < 15,537,393 MUST be marked as MSG-OUT-OF-SCOPE.
All four message types (GetBlockBodies 0x05, BlockBodies 0x06, GetReceipts 0x0f, Receipts 0x10) MUST undergo scope validation before processing.
An eth/70 client MUST never serve block bodies or receipts for any block with number < 15,537,393, regardless of the message type or requesting peer.

The checkpoint root provided for bootstrap initialization MUST be verified against a trusted source (weak subjectivity checkpoint). The LightClientBootstrap object MUST be cryptographically verified against this root before initializing the store.
Before accepting a bootstrap, the light client MUST verify that the bootstrap header root matches the trusted checkpoint root exactly. No partial matches or approximate verification is acceptable.
All LightClientUpdate objects MUST be validated to carry at least 2/3 supermajority of sync committee signatures before being applied to advance the light client's trusted state.
LightClientUpdate finalized header advancement MUST be verified: the finalized header in the update must be an ancestor of the attested header, proven via the finality branch Merkle proof.
Responses to bootstrap and update-by-range requests from peers MUST be cryptographically verified. Multiple peers SHOULD be queried to prevent eclipse attacks.

Each fork's dedicated specification document MUST define the exact field additions and transformations for light client data structures. The upgrade function MUST correctly map all fields from the previous fork format to the new fork format.
Full Node specs MUST define how full nodes prepare and serve light client data, while Sync Protocol specs MUST define how light clients consume it. These two halves MUST be consistent.
The light client MUST maintain a connection to at least one honest full node at all times. If all peers are disconnected, the light client MUST NOT consider its state as trustworthy.
After successful bootstrap (ACTION-BOOTSTRAP-LC), the light client store MUST contain a valid finalized header and the current sync committee. The state MUST transition to LC-BOOTSTRAPPED.

After processing a valid LightClientUpdate (ACTION-PROCESS-LC-UPDATE), the finalized header in the store MUST be advanced to the update's finalized header if it has a higher slot. The sync committee MUST be rotated if a new period boundary is crossed.
After processing a LightClientOptimisticUpdate, the optimistic head MUST be updated to the attested header. This MUST NOT affect the finalized header.

After detecting a fork epoch boundary (ACTION-DETECT-FORK-EPOCH) and upgrading the store (ACTION-UPGRADE-LC-STORE), the light client MUST operate with the new fork's data structures. No pre-fork structure fields may remain unupgraded.
The light client's finalized header MUST never regress to a lower slot. Once finalized, a header slot represents a monotonically non-decreasing minimum.

Before subscribing to gossip topics (ACTION-SUBSCRIBE-GOSSIP), the light client MUST have completed bootstrap and be in at least the BOOTSTRAPPED state, ensuring it can validate incoming gossip messages.
A corrupted sync committee supermajority (>= 2/3 dishonest) could sign invalid headers. The system MUST assume that fewer than 1/3 of sync committee members are Byzantine at any given time.
The eth_requestAccounts handler MUST require explicit user consent before exposing any account addresses. No accounts may be returned without user approval.
The consent dialog MUST be browser-isolated from DApp JavaScript manipulation. The DApp MUST NOT be able to programmatically approve, dismiss, or modify the dialog.
The consent dialog MUST accurately display the requesting origin to the user. Origin spoofing MUST be prevented by the provider implementation.
No maximum timeout is specified for user deliberation. Implementations MUST allow indefinite delay while user considers the request. Applications MUST handle the pending state gracefully.

After user rejection, repeated requests from the same origin MUST either re-display the dialog or immediately reject. Implementations SHOULD respect user fatigue and not facilitate consent-dialog spam.
Error objects returned on rejection MUST contain at minimum a descriptive message property. Standardized error codes from EIP-1193 SHOULD be used.
Users MUST be informed of the security implications of granting account access. The provider MUST NOT silently expose accounts to any origin.
After user approval, the resolved promise MUST contain an Array<string> with at least one valid Ethereum account address.
After user rejection, the promise MUST be rejected with an informative Error object. No account data may leak in the error.
Before processing eth_requestAccounts, the provider MUST check for window.ethereum availability. If not present, the flow MUST halt at STATE-PROVIDER-NOT-FOUND.

After caller context validation (ACTION-VALIDATE-CALLER-CONTEXT), the permission cache MUST be checked. If a cached permission exists for this origin, accounts MUST be returned without re-prompting the user.
Permission caching MUST be per-origin. An approval for origin A MUST NOT grant access to origin B.
After response validation (ACTION-VALIDATE-RESPONSE), if the response is empty or malformed, the system MUST transition to STATE-INVALID-RESPONSE rather than returning bad data to the DApp.
After evaluating a rejection reason, the system MUST generate distinct error objects for user-rejection, no-accounts-available, and provider-error cases. Each error MUST have a descriptive message.
The DApp (EXT-DAPP) MUST NOT be able to bypass the consent flow. All paths from DAPP-STARTED to ACCOUNTS-GRANTED MUST pass through STATE-AWAITING-USER-CONSENT or STATE-PERMISSION-CACHED.

After generating error objects (ACTION-GENERATE-ERROR-OBJECT) from any rejection path, the promise MUST be rejected. The error object MUST NOT contain any account addresses or private wallet information.
All transactions containing IO-heavy operations (SLOAD, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, CALL, CALLCODE, DELEGATECALL, SELFDESTRUCT) MUST have EIP-150 repriced gas costs applied at blocks >= 2,463,000.
The transaction pool and EVM gas metering MUST reject transactions that would exhaust resources through underpriced IO operations at post-Tangerine Whistle blocks.
Rate limiting MUST be applied to incoming transactions to prevent resource exhaustion even with correctly priced operations.

The specific gas cost values for IO-heavy operations MUST be sourced from EIP-150 directly. IO-heavy operations include: SLOAD, SSTORE, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODECOPY, CALL, CALLCODE, DELEGATECALL, and SELFDESTRUCT.

'IO-heavy operations' MUST be interpreted to include SLOAD, SSTORE, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODECOPY, CALL, CALLCODE, DELEGATECALL, and SELFDESTRUCT. No other operations are affected by this repricing.
All network participants (miners) MUST upgrade to fork-compatible client versions before block 2,463,000. Non-upgraded nodes will fork off and MUST be considered invalid.

The increased gas costs MUST accurately reflect the true computational cost of IO operations. If costs are misaligned, either DoS attacks remain viable (too low) or legitimate contracts become impractical (too high).
Attackers MUST NOT be able to find alternative underpriced operations to achieve similar DoS effects post-fork. The gas schedule MUST cover all resource-intensive operations.
After checking block number (ACTION-CHECK-BLOCK-NUMBER), if block < 2,463,000, the system MUST continue with pre-Tangerine Whistle gas rules. If block >= 2,463,000, EIP-150 rules MUST be applied.
After applying EIP-150 rules (ACTION-APPLY-EIP150-RULES), the system MUST transition to STATE-POST-TANGERINE and all subsequent blocks MUST use the new gas schedule.
After gas cost lookup (ACTION-LOOKUP-GAS-COST), the determined cost MUST be either the old (pre-TW) or new (post-TW) value. No intermediate or negotiated cost is valid.

After gas deduction (ACTION-DEDUCT-GAS), if remaining gas < 0, the transaction MUST transition to STATE-OUT-OF-GAS and the operation MUST revert. Otherwise the transaction continues with STATE-GAS-DEDUCTED.
After deploying the Tangerine Whistle fork (ACTION-DEPLOY-FORK), the DoS attack vector MUST be closed. Subsequent identical attack attempts MUST result in STATE-ATTACK-TOO-EXPENSIVE.
The fork activation at block 2,463,000 is irreversible. Once STATE-POST-TANGERINE is reached, the system MUST never revert to pre-Tangerine Whistle rules.

After an attacker crafts a malicious transaction pre-fork, the network MUST degrade to STATE-NETWORK-DEGRADED only if the underpriced operations exhaust node resources. Post-fork, the same attack MUST fail.
All incoming blocks from peers MUST have their difficulty validated against the expected difficulty computed using EIP-649 rules (fake block number with 3,000,000 offset for post-Byzantium blocks).
Block reward MUST be exactly 3 ETH (3e18 wei) for post-Byzantium blocks. Uncle rewards MUST use the formula (8-k) * 3 ETH / 8, and nephew reward MUST be 3 ETH / 32.
Fork activation block numbers MUST be checked during block processing. The block header MUST be fully validated including difficulty field before acceptance.
BYZANTIUM_FORK_BLKNUM MUST be defined in network configuration (4,370,000 for mainnet). This value MUST be used consistently across all difficulty and reward calculations.
The 3,000,000 block offset delay estimation (approximately 1.4 years at 15-second average block times) MUST be understood as an approximation. The actual delay depends on realized block times.
The difficulty bomb delay MUST provide sufficient time for Casper PoS development. If PoS is not ready when the delayed bomb activates, another delay EIP will be needed.
The reduced block reward (3 ETH vs 5 ETH) MUST maintain sufficient mining incentive for network security. Hashrate MUST remain at levels that prevent 51% attacks.
All clients MUST implement the difficulty calculation and reward changes identically. Any implementation difference will cause consensus failures between clients.
After checking Byzantium fork activation, if block_number >= BYZANTIUM_FORK_BLKNUM, the system MUST compute fake_block_number = max(0, block_number - 3,000,000) for the difficulty bomb.
After computing the fake block number, the ice age component MUST be calculated as 2^(fake_block // 100000 - 2). This exponential component is then added to the parent difficulty adjustment.
After computing final difficulty, the resulting difficulty MUST combine the parent difficulty adjustment with the bomb component. The result MUST be stored in STATE-DIFFICULTY-COMPUTED.
After comparing claimed vs expected difficulty, if they match the block MUST be accepted (STATE-DIFFICULTY-VALID). If they differ the block MUST be rejected (STATE-DIFFICULTY-INVALID).
After checking reward rules, if block >= BYZANTIUM_FORK_BLKNUM the base reward MUST be 3 ETH. If block < BYZANTIUM_FORK_BLKNUM the base reward MUST be 5 ETH.
After computing miner and uncle rewards, ACTION-CREDIT-COINBASE MUST add the total computed rewards to the miner's coinbase account. The state MUST transition to STATE-REWARDS-DISTRIBUTED.
The parent block data used for difficulty calculation MUST include valid parent_difficulty and parent_timestamp values. The fake block number MUST never be negative (enforced by max(0, ...)).
Before computing expected difficulty for validation, the block header received from a peer MUST contain a valid block number, parent hash, timestamp, and claimed difficulty field.
Before injecting the Ethereum provider, the page URL must resolve to a secure context where window.isSecureContext === true (HTTPS, localhost, or file://).
The URL origin navigated to must be validated as a potentially trustworthy origin per the W3C Secure Contexts specification before any provider injection occurs.
Before granting provider access to an iframe, the iframe's origin relationship to the parent page must be determined (first-party vs third-party).
Third-party iframes must be blocked from provider access by default; access is only permitted if the Permissions API explicitly grants it.
For first-party iframes, the sandbox attribute must either be absent or include 'allow-same-origin' before provider injection is permitted.
After the secure context check returns true, the system must be in the STATE-CONTEXT-SECURE state and proceed to origin trustworthiness verification.
After provider injection action completes successfully, window.ethereum must be defined and accessible to the page.
After an insecure context is detected, the provider must be blocked and window.ethereum must remain undefined.
After an untrustworthy origin is detected, the provider must be blocked regardless of the secure context status.
The browser must correctly implement and report window.isSecureContext at all times; wallet security checks depend on this value being accurate.
HTTPS origins presented to the wallet must have a valid certificate chain to a trusted root CA; provider injection must never occur on origins with invalid certificates.
Developer mode must default to disabled; HTTP localhost provider access is only permitted when the user has explicitly enabled developer mode.
An attacker must not be able to compromise the localhost development environment; if dev mode is enabled and localhost is compromised, the attacker gains full provider access.
After sandbox restriction is detected on a first-party iframe, provider access must be blocked.
After a third-party iframe receives explicit permission via the Permissions API, provider access must be allowed.
After a third-party iframe permission is denied, provider access must be blocked and window.ethereum must be undefined in that iframe.
After a compatible sandbox configuration is verified on a first-party iframe, provider access must be allowed.
The origin classification of an iframe (first-party vs third-party) must be determined by comparing the iframe origin against the parent page origin using same-origin policy rules.
Before accepting a BLS-to-execution-change gossip message, the node must verify that current_epoch >= CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH using wall-clock time.
Before accepting a BLS-to-execution-change message, the node must verify this is the first valid change received for the given validator index (per-node deduplication).
Before accepting a BLS-to-execution-change message, the full process_bls_to_execution_change validation must pass including BLS signature verification.
Before processing a beacon block received via gossip, the fork digest in the topic must match the expected Capella fork digest.
Before serving a block response, the fork version must be correctly determined via compute_fork_version for the block's epoch to ensure proper serialization format.

Block request serialization format must match the determined fork version; GENESIS_FORK_VERSION maps to phase0, ALTAIR_FORK_VERSION to altair, BELLATRIX_FORK_VERSION to bellatrix, CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION to capella.
After epoch threshold check fails (current_epoch < CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH), the BLS change message must be ignored and not forwarded.
After all validation passes for a BLS-to-execution-change message, it must be accepted for future block inclusion and forwarded to gossip peers.
After validation failure in process_bls_to_execution_change, the message must be rejected and not forwarded to peers.
After fork digest verification fails, the beacon block gossip message must be rejected.
After block serialization completes for any fork version, the serialized response must be sent to the requesting peer.
After fork digest and block content validation both pass, the Capella beacon block must be accepted for further processing.
Wall-clock time used for epoch calculation must be reasonably synchronized across nodes; clock skew must not cause incorrect acceptance or rejection of BLS change messages.
An attacker must not be able to forge valid BLS signatures for bls_to_execution_change messages; doing so would enable redirecting withdrawal credentials to attacker-controlled addresses.
The scope of 'first valid change per validator' deduplication is per-node: each node independently tracks which validator indices have had a valid BLS change message accepted.
Capella gossip topic transitions must follow the same mechanics as Altair fork transitions; topics must be switched at the correct epoch boundary.
Before executing a padding operation, the size parameter must be a valid non-negative integer that is convertible via int().
Before executing padding with an untrusted size input, bounds checking must ensure the size parameter does not exceed reasonable limits to prevent memory exhaustion.
Callers of byte padding functions must provide size values that are semantically correct for the byte data being processed (e.g., 32 for EVM words, 20 for addresses).
After left padding completes, the result byte array must have exactly 'size' bytes with the original value right-justified and zero bytes on the left.
After right padding completes, the result byte array must have exactly 'size' bytes with the original value left-justified and zero bytes on the right.
After checking value length when value length >= target size, the original value must be returned unmodified (no truncation occurs).
After size conversion completes, the integer size value must be ready for use in padding operations.
After executing padding on an untrusted size input, memory must be allocated based on the size parameter for the padded result.
Padding operations must never truncate data; if the value length exceeds the target size, the original value is returned unchanged.
Sufficient memory must be available to allocate the padded result; the system must handle memory exhaustion gracefully for extremely large size values.
Padding bytes must always be zero bytes (0x00); no other fill value is permitted for left_pad_zero_bytes or right_pad_zero_bytes.
The size parameter must accept int, FixedUnsigned, or Uint types; the int() conversion must handle all three correctly.
Before importing an interchange file, the validator client must be completely stopped and not signing any messages.
Before processing the interchange file contents, the JSON must be validated against the required schema format.
Before merging records, all BLS public keys in the interchange file must be validated as proper BLS12-381 public keys.
Before signing a block proposal, the block slot must be checked against the slashing protection database to ensure no conflicting block exists at the same slot.
Before signing a block, the block slot must be >= the minimum previously signed slot in the slashing protection database.
Before signing an attestation, the source epoch must be >= the minimum previously signed source epoch and the target epoch must be >= the minimum previously signed target epoch.
Before merging imported records, the genesis_validators_root in the interchange file must match the current network's genesis_validators_root.
After a block is signed, the slot and signing root must be recorded in the slashing protection database before any further signing operations.
After an attestation is signed, the source epoch, target epoch, and signing root must be recorded in the slashing protection database.
After genesis root mismatch is detected, the import must be rejected entirely; no partial merge is permitted.
After successful record merge, the slashing protection database must contain the union of existing and imported records with maximum slot/epoch values used for floors.
After a block conflict is detected (same slot, different signing root), signing must be refused to prevent a slashable offense.
After a surround vote is detected in attestation checking, signing must be refused to prevent a slashable offense.
Missing signing_root in imported records must be treated as potential conflicts; the validator must refuse to sign at the same slot/epoch when signing_root is absent.
Duplicate public keys appearing in the interchange data array must be merged by combining all their signed_blocks and signed_attestations records; conflicting records must cause import rejection.
An attacker must not be able to trigger file import while the validator is actively signing; import and signing operations must be mutually exclusive.
The interchange file must not have been maliciously modified; a tampered file that omits critical historical records could allow slashable signing.
After signing roots format verification detects missing roots, conservative protection must be applied before data is trusted for import.
After block slot is below the minimum floor, signing must be rejected.
After source or target epoch is below the minimum floor, attestation signing must be rejected.
After JSON schema validation fails, the interchange file must be rejected and no records imported.
Before processing a provider.request() call, the RequestArguments object must contain a valid 'method' field as a non-empty string.
Before forwarding a request to the Wallet, all input data from the DApp must be sanitized to prevent injection or malformed data attacks.
Before processing a request, rate limiting must be checked to prevent resource exhaustion from excessive DApp requests.
Before establishing a connection, the chainId must be verified and represented in hexadecimal string format as per the specification.
Before exposing account addresses to a DApp, explicit user authorization must be obtained through an authorization flow.
After request validation fails, the promise must be rejected with a ProviderRpcError containing the appropriate error code.
After the Wallet successfully processes a request, the promise must resolve with the RPC method result delivered back to the DApp.
After the Provider transitions to disconnected state, a 'disconnect' event must be emitted with a ProviderRpcError.
After a chain switch occurs, a 'chainChanged' event must be emitted with the new chainId in hex format and the provider must remain in connected state.
After user revokes account access, the accounts array must become empty and an 'accountsChanged' event must be emitted.
After an error condition is detected, the ProviderRpcError must be constructed with the correct standardized error code (4001, 4100, 4200, 4900, or 4901).
The Provider must never contain private user data (private keys, seed phrases); the Provider and Wallet programs must remain isolated from each other at all times.
The browser must provide adequate isolation between DApp JavaScript and Provider internals; DApps must not be able to directly access Provider internal state.
Attackers must not be able to modify the Provider object after it is exposed at window.ethereum; modifications could enable interception of user credentials or transactions.
The ProviderRpcError 'data' property, when present, must be JSON-serializable contextual information; no specific structure is required but it must not leak internal implementation details.
When multiple chains are connected, eth_chainId must return the active/default chain; switching must be explicit via wallet_switchEthereumChain.
After an account change occurs (user selects different account), an 'accountsChanged' event must be emitted with the updated accounts array.
Event listeners must be properly managed; DApps should remove listeners on unmount to prevent memory leaks and stale event handler behavior.
After a validated request passes security checks and rate limiting, it must be securely forwarded to the Wallet with Provider-Wallet isolation maintained.
After the Wallet returns an error, the promise must be rejected with a ProviderRpcError delivered to the DApp.
